disputed: Lang has denied the January 6 assault allegations as self-defense, and none of his January 6 charges were ever tested at trial due to the pardon. Whether he meets the specific legal or scholarly definition of 'white supremacist' is a characterization used by NBC News and some commentators based on his statements and associations (including organizing a self-described 'national constitutional militia'), not a court finding. The post-pardon arrests (Minnesota, DC, Texas) are pending or resolved by plea/bond, not final convictions, as of the most recent reporting.

items: Since his pardon, Lang has organized rallies, announced a run for Congress for the Florida Senate seat vacated by Marco Rubio, and remained a vocal pro-Trump, pro-ICE influencer. (Newsweek (https://www.newsweek.com/who-is-jake-lang-pardoned-jan-6-protester-who-kicked-over-anti-ice-sign-11475624))

February 2026: arrested in Minnesota after posting video of himself kicking down a 'Prosecute ICE' sculpture, saying on camera 'our country was made for Americans, not Somalis' and 'Pro ICE baby, America First, America Only'; charged with a felony for the roughly $6,000 in property damage. (Newsweek (https://www.newsweek.com/who-is-jake-lang-pardoned-jan-6-protester-who-kicked-over-anti-ice-sign-11475624))

March 2026: charged in DC Superior Court after being recorded telling a Metropolitan Police commander who had confronted him at the Capitol on January 6 that the officer should be 'put down like a dead dog' and 'hung' in front of the Capitol, allegedly adding 'public execution is the only solution for animals like you.' NBC News's report on this charge describes Lang as 'a white supremacist and pro-Trump influencer.' (NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/jan-6-rioter-jake-lang-arrested-threat-dc-police-officer-rcna261395))

June 2026: arrested in Dallas, Texas on a felony charge of making a terroristic threat, after Karmelo Anthony's family alleged Lang threatened to shoot Anthony (then on trial for murder) in the head if he was not convicted. Lang was released on $250,000 bond with an order to leave Texas within 24 hours except for court appearances. (CBS News (https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jake-lang-far-right-influencer-arrested-texas-charge-terroristic-threats/); FOX 4 Dallas (https://www.fox4news.com/news/jan-6-rioter-jake-lang-released-bond-ordered-leave-texas-within-24-hours))
sections.label: Post-pardon pattern

summary: Edward Jacob 'Jake' Lang is a far-right activist federally charged with 11 counts related to the January 6, 2021 Capitol attack, including allegations he assaulted police officers with a baseball bat and riot shield. He spent nearly four years in pretrial detention - one of a small number of January 6 defendants held pretrial, which a Trump-appointed judge justified at the time by calling the evidence against him 'very strong' and citing his 'overt expressions of willingness to use violence in the future.' He was never convicted; Trump pardoned him along with more than 1,500 other January 6 defendants on his first day back in office, January 20, 2025, before Lang's case went to trial.
title: Jake Lang: pardoned January 6 defendant's post-pardon conduct
